scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Gloving is believed to have started in the 1990s and early 2000s, evolving from the use of glow sticks at raves.
Early practitioners used white gloves that reflected black light before LED technology became standard.
Video evidence of the modern form exists from 2006.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a form of rave entertainment, gloving has evolved into a competitive hobby and a digital subculture.
It carries meanings of self-expression and technical skill.
Recent internet memes have introduced satirical concepts like 'Gloving Wars' and 'degloving' as a symbolic ban from the community.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: MagicMtn Gloving 057: Happy Mother's Day - All You Need To Know (JVNA Remix). (https://archive.org/details/magic-mtn-gloving-057-happy-mothers-day-all-you-need-to-know-jvna-remix)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed primarily with the hands and fingers.

It incorporates 'liquiding' (fluid arm movements), 'finger-tutting' (geometric finger shapes), and 'popping.' Dancers use fingertip LED lights to accentuate patterns, often performing 'light-shows' for a single viewer.
The technique involves applying hip-hop dance concepts to the small-scale movements of the fingers and wrists.
Watch for Finger-tutting, Liquiding.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (4uafkkjy-EU)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Intimate, focused on the 'box' of space directly in front of the viewer.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Gloving is performed to electronic dance music.
The primary 'instruments' are specialized gloves equipped with LED microlights.
Listen for the Synthesizers, Drum machines, Digital samplers.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 135 beats a minute.
The sound is characterized by the synthesized textures and heavy basslines of EDM. The dance responds to the 'drop'—a moment of high intensity—and the intricate percussive elements of the track.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The essential costume consists of white or black gloves with LED lights at the fingertips.
The setting is typically a dark environment, such as a rave or music festival, to maximize the visibility of the lights.
The performance is often intimate, with the dancer and viewer in close proximity.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The California-based company EmazingLights is a central entity in the gloving world, having appeared on Shark Tank and becoming a major manufacturer of the equipment.
Pasquale Rotella, CEO of Insomniac Events, is a notable figure for his role in banning the dance from mainstream EDM events.
While specific regional styles are not detailed in the sources, the dance is heavily concentrated in the electronic music scenes of North America, particularly California.
Gloving is a subclass of modern dance and is influenced by hip-hop styles including liquiding, finger-tutting, and popping.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Gloving is influence of Finger-tutting: Gloving applies finger-tutting techniques to an LED-enhanced performance.
Gloving is influence of Liquiding: The fluid arm and hand movements of liquiding are a core component of gloving.
Gloving is influence of Popping: Rhythmic 'hits' from popping are used to accentuate beats in a light-show.

scenes.title: Common mistakes and what to avoid
narration: Avoid blocking the lights with the palms; ensure movements are large enough to be seen but contained within the viewer's field of vision.
Teachers of this dance warn against: not bending wrists back 90 degrees, resulting in smaller circles and sloppy illusions
Teachers of this dance warn against: having palms facing outward to the sides instead of directly toward the viewer receiving the light show
Teachers of this dance warn against: rushing the finger rolls before building muscle memory

steps_as_taught.name: Whips
steps_as_taught.description: Starting from an L-shaped tut position, roll the hand outward into an open hand and back in to create circular light motion.

steps_as_taught.name: Backward Whips
steps_as_taught.description: Starting facing inward, unroll the hand outward and spin to return back into tut position.

steps_as_taught.name: Tunnels
steps_as_taught.description: A two-handed whip concept executing stacked alternating finger rolls moving outward and inward.

steps_as_taught.name: Upward Finger Roll
steps_as_taught.description: Opening and closing fingers one by one starting from the thumbs while facing upward.
